surface: /winter/ home, desktop 1440x900 (second comp for composition A)
composition: Desktop A: full facade centred with lawn and oaks, headline in the snow left of the walk, hanging wooden signs under the portals, Choose a room section starting at the bottom edge.
prompt: A desktop landing page, landscape, for Wander Niagara, rendered edge to edge as a real web page with crisp readable text, no browser window or device around it. The page is a house: the visitor is planning a winter day trip or overnight to St. Catharines and the Benchlands and picks a room to enter. Parts in reading order: a slim header on the night sky with a small white "Wander" wordmark at left, four small white text links "Eat and drink", "Outdoors", "Stay", "Stories" in the middle, and one small engraved brass door plaque button "What's on" at right. Below it the whole symmetrical red-brick Georgian colonial at night, five bays wide with two dormers, centred between two bare oaks on a snowy lawn, seen straight on from the front walk at a slight low angle; every window glows warm amber through sheer curtains with a candle in each, the left ground-floor window showing a crystal chandelier and the right a lit Christmas tree; warm-white mini-lights outline every window and the white arched portico; a wreath with a red velvet bow on the black six-panel door, a lit brass lantern, lit shrubs along the foundation, snow on the roof, slow falling snow. Under each of the two ground-floor windows and under the door hangs a small wooden sign on two chains, lettered "Eat, drink and shop", "What's on this winter", "Winter outdoors". In the blue-shadowed snow of the lawn, to the left of the walk, set as type: the headline "Winter is made for wandering" and the subline "A holiday escape to St. Catharines and the Benchlands." Along the very bottom edge a page section begins with a thin brass rule and the heading "Choose a room". Visual law: a warm navy night sky, never black. A heavy, friendly 1990 greeting-card serif in snow white. Brass plaques with engraved lettering. Warm inside, cold outside; film-grain warmth.
